issues.description: AlterTable grammar complects per-action parsing with multi-action delimiting; collapsing the outer Delimited drops legitimate multi-clause ALTER TABLE syntax.
issues.detail: The previous shape allowed `ALTER TABLE t ADD col ..., DROP COLUMN x` (a real, removed test case). Replacing outer Delimited with a single OneOf says ALTER TABLE has exactly one action. That is the wrong fact about the world. Decompose: one rule for an action, a separate Delimited wrapping actions. Don't delete the example to make the grammar fit.

issues.description: SignedSegmentGrammar attached to numeric literals is place-oriented; the value `-2147483648` is one negative integer, not a sign concept next to a positive one.
issues.detail: Identity seed should be a signed numeric literal (a value). Modeling it as an optional sign sibling beside a NumericLiteralSegment complects lexical tokens with the semantic value. Either teach NumericLiteralSegment to carry sign in this position, or introduce a SignedNumericLiteral value. The current shape will keep recurring across the dialect.

issues.description: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE accepting NumericLiteralSegment widens the grammar without a cited fact about T-SQL.
issues.detail: DEFAULT_LANGUAGE takes a language name or lcid alias, not arbitrary numeric literals at this position per the documented syntax. Adding NumericLiteralSegment to the OneOf is an easy fix that hides whether the underlying fact is true. Either cite the lcid case and constrain it, or drop the numeric branch.

issues.description: Inner DROP COLUMN list-inside-list shape allows ambiguous nesting like `DROP COLUMN a, b, COLUMN c`.
issues.detail: The new `DROP` branch wraps `COLUMN <Delimited cols>` inside another Delimited. That structure permits a single DROP to contain a delimited list of column refs and then more `COLUMN ...` clauses, mixing two different syntaxes T-SQL keeps separate. Pick one: repeat `COLUMN col` per item, or one `COLUMN` with delimited cols. Not both nested.

issues.description: Test fixture removal is the tell; deleted case `ADD ... , DROP COLUMN ...` was the load-bearing evidence and is now gone.
issues.detail: Removing a passing fixture to make a refactor pass is exactly the kind of TDD-as-design failure mode to flag. The fixture documented a real T-SQL form. If the new grammar genuinely cannot parse it, that is a regression to call out in the PR description, not a silent deletion.

review.summary: The refactor of AlterTableStatementSegment trades one form of complexity for another and silently regresses multi-action ALTER TABLE by deleting the fixture that proved it worked. The new shape conflates "one action" with "many actions" by collapsing the outer Delimited, then re-introduces inner Delimiteds per branch with ambiguous nesting. Identity seed sign handling is place-oriented rather than modeled as a signed value. DEFAULT_LANGUAGE widens to numeric literals without a cited fact. The CREATE LOGIN and table-variable-index additions themselves are SIMPLE and well-scoped; the ALTER TABLE rewrite is COMPLECTED and EASY-NOT-SIMPLE.
